rows.note: Timing chain failure, no coolant symptom. Teacher is right.
A malfunctioning instrument cluster is a named electrical component. Gold is right, teacher too conservative.

Diagnosed parts are rear axle seals, bearings, and gears -- differential/driveline components, which our POWER TRAIN definition explicitly covers ('driveline/axle'), not ride/handling suspension parts. Teacher is right.
Evaporative canister (a fuel-system emissions component) explicitly diagnosed. Teacher is right, gold too general.
Mud flaps causing ice buildup that impairs steering -- a named accessory part. Teacher is right, gold too conservative.
Explicit 'battery coolant for hybrid system failed' on a 4xe hybrid -- the rare hybrid-propulsion category. Neither original answer is right.

REVISED after 5/5 models independently chose EXTERIOR LIGHTING: the complainant's central stated concern (rule 2) is 'you can't tell your headlights are off' -- a headlight-indication problem, i.e. EXTERIOR LIGHTING -- even though the root design cause is the always-on dash panel. Both are defensible; EXTERIOR LIGHTING is now primary.
'Put in park' refers to the transmission gear selector, not the parking/emergency brake -- a Park-pawl failure. Gold is right, teacher misread the word 'park.'

Catalytic converter and emissions sensors are the named cause -- per the confirmed exhaust/emissions convention (gotcha B16), this routes to ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING, not fuel delivery or plain ENGINE.
Three genuinely distinct, unrelated problems: a door that won't open (latch), an A/C compressor failing repeatedly (standalone AC unit), and intermittent wipers.
Power steering assist and stability/traction control are both explicitly named as failing together, twice -- likely a shared module, genuinely dual.

Explicitly quotes recall '(AIR BAGS, ELECTRICAL SYSTEM)' [14V373000]; the stalling the next day is consistent with the same underlying electrical/ignition fault, not an independent transmission problem.
A jack that doesn't extend high enough -- vehicle accessory equipment. Teacher is right; gold's raw answer isn't even a valid category.
A leaking window seal is a physical body/window-component defect; no electrical failure has actually occurred, only a feared future risk. Teacher is right, gold is speculative.
ABS failure on a passenger Neon, no air-brake context. Gold is right.

Same terse, no-symptom dashboard-crack-near-airbag pattern as the confirmed 1346344 (no deployment fear or airbag malfunction stated, just location) -- STRUCTURE, not AIR BAGS. Neither original answer is right.
ABS-related brake failure on a passenger pickup, no air-brake context. Gold is right.
Dealer specifically diagnosed the brake actuator (a hydraulic/ABS modulator component). Teacher is right, gold too general.

A broad electrical/instrument cascade (ABS light, cruise, speedometer, wipers all malfunctioning) plus a separate, real brake-seizure event with a burning smell. Cruise control (gold) is only one minor symptom among many.
ABS failure on a passenger Blazer. Gold is right.

Repeated stalling with power-steering/brake loss as a downstream consequence; the dealer explicitly found nothing and no component is named. Same reasoning as 2016886. Neither original answer is confirmed.

Two things are named as equally 'life threatening': ABS (a brake-family issue) and unexplained power loss (no component named, matching UNKNOWN OR OTHER). Teacher's POWER TRAIN has no textual support.

Confirmed diagnostic code P2111 (throttle stuck open) and throttle body replacement -- matches the established throttle-body convention exactly. The transmission mention is an unrelated historical repair. Teacher is right.
Classic 'Ford death wobble' explicitly naming both suspension and steering -- the same established boundary ambiguity.
Dealer's actual repair recommendation explicitly named a thermostat replacement (a cooling-system part). Gold is right, teacher too conservative given a specific repair was named.
A severe sudden-acceleration crash where the brakes were applied but did nothing -- the same dual acceleration/brake-failure pattern as 1056493 and 2148719.
An HVAC blower motor (electrical component) recalled for fire risk -- not an engine part. Teacher is right, gold is wrong.
Two distinct, independently detailed problems: unreplaced Takata airbags, and separately seized brake calipers requiring a $3000 repair.

The clockspring/airbag/horn/cruise cluster is the complainant's explicitly stated primary concern ('why is Chrysler not being made to rectify at least the air bag (clock spring) issue'), while ongoing dash flickering/radio issues are a separate real electrical symptom. A third issue (front hub replacement) is dropped as a minor aside.
Five repeated unintended-acceleration events, one fatal-risk crash into a tree. Gold's STRUCTURE has no support -- the tree isn't part of the vehicle. Teacher is right.
Front wheel spinning up with a 'tracking light' illuminating -- a traction-control malfunction, not a wheel/rim defect. Neither original answer is right.
Difficulty engaging Park on the gear selector -- same pattern as 1185049. No steering symptom is described. Teacher is right, gold has no support.
A corroded tail-light socket causing the light itself to fail to illuminate -- the lighting itself is the stated problem. Teacher is right.
Explicit ABS-module diagnosis on a passenger Fusion -- a hydraulic-system component, no air-brake context. Neither original answer is precise; hydraulic is the clear best fit.

Smoke visibly originating from and escalating within the engine compartment while the truck was running -- reasonable location evidence for an engine-bay fire, unlike 105591 where investigators explicitly called the cause undetermined. Gold is right.
Emission-system warning, shaking, severe misfiring -- purely an engine/emissions performance issue with zero lane-keeping content. Gold appears to be a data-join error. Teacher is right.

A known Toyota throttle-body failure causing a sudden stall -- the throttle body is an air-intake/throttle-control part, not fuel delivery, and matches the established throttle-body convention. Teacher is right.
GM Ecotec piston-ring oil-consumption defect progressing to white smoke and shaking -- an internal engine defect, no drivetrain symptom. Teacher is right.
Two distinct, detailed, real issues: a fuel-pump-cutoff spray-back defect explicitly involving 'gas,' and a disputed airbag-frontal recall exclusion. Both genuinely present.
Repeated generic brake repairs and a seizing event, no subtype-specific detail.

Explicitly quotes the infamous GM ignition-switch recall '(AIR BAGS, ELECTRICAL SYSTEM)' [14V047000]; power-steering/window loss and the key lodging in the switch are downstream symptoms of that same ignition-switch defect, not an independent steering problem.
Named high-pressure fuel line/pump hose-clamp failure on a gas Mercedes. Teacher is right, gold too general.
The described behavior (stuttering/stalling on takeoff, in stop-and-go traffic) is a dual-clutch-transmission clutch-engagement characteristic, explicitly named as the DCT. Teacher is right.
Recall text explicitly and repeatedly says 'mechanical (cable) type parking brake' and 'parking brake actuator shaft.' Teacher is right, gold too general.
A known roof-antenna seal leak (body/roof component), not a windshield/visibility issue and no electrical failure has occurred. Teacher is right, gold too conservative.
Explicit, repeated brake-line pressure loss. Teacher is right, gold too general.
Vehicle 'wanders' with no specific part named -- the same directional-stability ambiguity as the death-wobble boundary cases.
Exhaust manifold, per the confirmed exhaust-system convention (gotcha B16). Gold is right.
Two distinct real harms in one crash: ABS brake failure causing the collision (hydraulic, no air-brake context), and airbag deployment causing burn injuries.
Explicit 'bad brake booster' diagnosis. Teacher is right, gold too general.
Confirmed complete engine lockup, matching a known engine recall. Teacher is right, gold is far too generic.

Extensive hybrid-specific language ('sluggish in both hybrid and electric modes,' a replaced electric coolant heater for the hybrid battery) -- the rare hybrid-propulsion category. Neither original answer is right.
A horn-button ergonomic/design complaint doesn't fit EQUIPMENT's aftermarket-accessory definition, and no other category covers OEM horn switches. Gold is right.
'See attached document' -- zero textual content to classify from. Teacher is right.
Windshield and side-window cracking, no wiper involvement at all. Teacher is right, gold misapplied the wiper subtype.

A dozen-plus ADAS/system warnings cascaded after a service visit; the diagnostic explicitly found 'excessive air to brake' among other things. Gold's LANE DEPARTURE (one light among dozens) doesn't fit at all.
'Would not start' with a repair cost mentioned but the actual failed part never named, and zero steering content anywhere. Neither original answer is confirmed by the text.

Miss/hesitation/stall at a specific RPM range with no fuel-delivery component (pump/injector/tank) ever named -- a general engine-performance complaint. Teacher is right, gold overspecified without evidence.
